skill.name: Plan
skill.prompt:
## Plan

Produce a complete, concise implementation plan for the current Goal Round. Choose the planning method appropriate to the work. For behavior changes, identify the underlying cause, governing concept or invariant, and existing owner before listing edits. Prefer strengthening an existing concept; introduce one only when it clarifies the behavior and reduces special cases. Do not change repository files. 

### Guidance

- Thrashing is a real danger with AI agents. To mitigate this, consider if the Goal is merely a symptom of a missing or misused concept in the target app architecture. Feel free to explore other Goals to determine if they have additional insights into this question.
- Over- or under-specificity can also cause undesirable implementation outcomes. Ensure that the plan has the information it needs for effective implementation, but not unnecessary details.
- Always use plain language.

### Format

Return an actionable plan with stable checklist IDs and meaningful verification.

Example:
Task #1 - short description of the work (what) and the rationale (why)
Task #2 - short description of the work (what) and the rationale (why)
(etc.)

### Intent and architecture

Review Refine's relevant documentation files under Refine's runtime at `<refine-runtime>/docs/intent/***/*.*` as the durable product specification.

default-plan.summary:
Cause and governing concept: Controls combined application settings with operational Skill and Site entry points. The existing browser shell owns navigation placement, shared styling, and dropdown interaction; Skills and Knowledge Hub already own their lists, creation, execution, and management. Strengthen that separation without introducing a new domain concept or duplicating those capabilities.

Task #1 - Preserve and assess the retained implementation. Start from f3945f54 and 0a85e69c, checking the requirements below against current code. Keep completed work and make only necessary corrections; the older report’s description of an uncommitted helper fix is superseded by Git evidence.

Task #2 - Confirm shell structure and wording. In static/index.html and shared navigation styles, ensure right-aligned actions appear as Skills, Sites, Settings, and + New Goal. Move Skill and Site lists out of Settings. Retain Settings’ context selectors, status, configuration, appearance, update, and utility actions. Preserve New Goal’s related actions and existing routes. Update remaining user-facing Controls references and relevant intent documentation consistently.

Task #3 - Confirm each menu uses its existing feature owner. In settings_skills.js, show enabled Custom Skills for the active node, followed by a separator and New Skill / Manage Skills. Reuse the existing editor, typed input preflight, and agent-tab launch; management goes to #/settings/skills. In knowledge-hub.js, show Sites, followed by a separator and New Site / Manage Sites. Reuse site creation and existing draft/published opening behavior; management goes to #/settings/knowledge-hub. Keep creation and management available when lists are empty or fail. Preserve refresh on opening, definition changes, and context changes, rejecting stale responses.

Task #4 - Verify shared interaction and layout. Keep menu dismissal and mutual exclusion in common.js and reuse existing summary, row, icon, separator, panel, and spacing styles. Verify keyboard opening, Escape with focus restoration, outside-click and action dismissal, and scrollable panels within the viewport at desktop and narrow widths in both themes. Correct any gaps through these existing owners.

Task #5 - Validate the retained candidate and resolve the Quality evidence. Run tests/web_topbar_navigation.test.js with Chromium available, plus affected Knowledge Hub, screen-render, Skill-launch, and Node-context tests and the Rust static navigation contract. Confirm order, exclusive placement, separators, creation, management destinations, Skill inputs, draft and published links, empty/error lists, refresh races, and preserved Settings controls. Skipped browser tests do not establish success. Recover the exact identities and output of the 12 reported broader Rust failures, reproduce them, and compare against the implementation parent where necessary. Fix candidate-caused regressions; document unrelated baseline failures separately without weakening tests or claiming a full pass. Hand off the exact tested candidate and remaining limitations to Quality.
evidence: Reviewed project-root intent documentation for navigation, shared components, Skills, and Knowledge Hub, plus the retained worktree’s updated navigation specification.
Implementation commit f3945f54 already contains the requested navigation changes and regression tests.
Quality commit 0a85e69c contains the terminal browser helper correction. The current worktree is clean.
Inspected existing menu interaction handlers, Skill rendering and launch behavior, and navigation tests. No files changed or tests run during planning.
